workflows.title: List hosts
workflows.summary: Hosts, quorum, votes, control node, and QDevice registration.
workflows.description: Reads cluster membership, quorum, and registry host slots through one reachable member, then checks SSH from this workstation to every host. Takes seconds.

params.label: Skip the SSH check from this workstation

workflows.title: List guests
workflows.summary: Production and staging VMs with live state, HA, replication, and addresses.
workflows.description: Reads the BMAC registry and live Proxmox VM, HA, and replication state through one reachable member.

workflows.title: List VM slots
workflows.summary: Every fixed production and staging address, who uses it, its FQDNs, and the Cloudflare DNS records each domain needs.
workflows.description: Lists the VM slots cluster.conf reserves, the registered guest in each (read from the registry through one reachable host), the FQDNs the Cloudflare Tunnel routes to each slot, and the proxied CNAME records each production domain needs. Changes nothing.

params.label: Use cluster.conf only (don't read the registry)

workflows.title: List replication jobs
workflows.summary: Every replication job's last sync, next sync, and failures.
workflows.description: Reads every online host's Proxmox replication status through one reachable member.

params.label: Production VM
params.help: Only show the jobs of this production VM.

workflows.title: List storage
workflows.summary: Every host's ZFS pool health and capacity and Proxmox storage.
workflows.description: Reads every online host's ZFS pools and Proxmox storage through one reachable member. Flags pools with less than 10% free.

params.label: Host
params.help: Only show this host.

workflows.title: List disks
workflows.summary: Every host's pool vdevs with LUKS state, and every disk outside a pool with its status.
workflows.description: Reads every online host directly over SSH: each pool vdev's state, encryption, and member disks with serial and size, and every disk outside a pool, whether it is available, awaiting retirement finalization, or part of an interrupted add or replace. Never finalizes anything; use Inventory disks for that.

params.label: Host
params.help: Only show this host.

workflows.title: Cluster health check
workflows.summary: Hosts, corosync links, QDevice, every ZFS member, free space, and SMART.
workflows.description: Inspects every host directly (or through another member), every corosync link between hosts, the QDevice, every ZFS pool and vdev member with disk serials, rpool free space, and each drive's SMART health. Guests are not inspected. Takes a minute or more.

workflows.title: Full cluster state
workflows.summary: Exhaustive read-only report of every host, the QDevice, and the registry.
workflows.description: Runs the complete read-only diagnostic snapshot on every reachable host and the QDevice: identity, networking, SSH trust, quorum, services, ISO readiness, HA, replication, ZFS, LUKS, SMART, boot, nftables, the guest gateway and egress fallback, the tunnel replica, and the shared registry. Produces a very long report and takes several minutes.

workflows.title: Inspect a host
workflows.summary: One host's configuration, guests, replicas, and rpool layout with disk serials.
workflows.description: Shows one Proxmox host's configuration, the guests it runs and the replicas it stores, and its rpool layout: every vdev resolved to physical disk serials, the boot/ESP vdev, device-removal progress, unused disks, and per-zvol usage.

workflows.title: Inspect a production VM
workflows.summary: One production VM across HA, replication, routing, storage, QGA, and SSH.
workflows.description: Checks one registered production VM without changing guest, Proxmox, HA, replication, route, or registry configuration.

workflows.title: Inspect the QDevice
workflows.summary: Whether a QDevice is needed, registered, alive, and voting on every host.
workflows.description: Reports whether the cluster needs an external QDevice, whether one is registered, and whether every member sees it alive and voting, and explains how to repair or replace it.

workflows.title: Check QDevice access
workflows.summary: Whether this workstation reaches the prepared QDevice as root over SSH.
workflows.description: Checks that ssh root@PROXMOX_QDEVICE_HOST works from this workstation with strict host key checking. Needs no cluster member, so it works before the first Proxmox host is set up. Takes seconds.

workflows.title: Monitoring state
workflows.summary: Every node's Healthchecks check, last ping, and open problems.
workflows.description: Reads this cluster's Healthchecks.io checks and every monitored node's agent (Proxmox hosts, the QDevice, and active production VMs) over SSH, and lists open problems, checks no node uses, and the check budget. Needs MONITORING_ENABLED=true. Changes nothing.

workflows.title: Send a test alert
workflows.summary: Make one node send a labelled test pulse through its Healthchecks check.
workflows.description: Runs the monitor agent's test pulse on one node: a DOWN email marked bmacevent and an UP email marked bmacclear, to test your Gmail filters and Pushover. Nothing in the cluster changes.

params.label: Node
params.help: moxN, qdevice, or prodN. Asked for when empty.

workflows.title: Inventory disks
workflows.summary: Every physical disk, pool vdev, and disk that is safe to pull.
workflows.description: Inventories every physical disk on a host with serial and exact capacity, every pool vdev and member, and disks that are safe to remove. When a decommission has finished evacuating, it asks before finalizing the retirement of those disks.
workflows.notes: Normally read-only. It changes the host only if you approve finalizing a completed decommission.

workflows.title: Add production VM
workflows.summary: Allocate the next prodN, install its OS, replicate it, and enable HA.
workflows.description: Allocates the next prodN, installs its OS, verifies guest identity and SSH, creates replication to every selected placement host, configures HA, and adds its FQDNs (and its staging slots' FQDNs) to every host's Cloudflare Tunnel config. It can resume its own incomplete allocation after a failure. Start with a dry run.

workflows.title: Remove production VM
workflows.summary: Permanently destroy a production VM and everything BMAC owns for it.
workflows.description: Permanently removes one production VM after exact identity validation: HA resource and rule, replication jobs and target copies, the VM and its volumes, orchestration metadata, and its registry allocation, then removes its FQDNs from the Cloudflare Tunnel config. Staging VMs derived from it must be removed first.

params.label: Dry run (show the destruction plan only)

workflows.title: Record where production VMs run
workflows.summary: After a failover, record each production VM's current host as its owner. Moves nothing.
workflows.description: Compares the registry owner and replication targets of every active production VM with where Proxmox runs it and replicates it, and (without dry run) records the live values in the registry. Use it when the dashboard reports that a production VM runs on a different host than its registry owner. No VM is moved, stopped, or restarted, and a VM with a move or resize in progress is left alone.

workflows.title: Move production VM
workflows.summary: Relocate a production VM to another of its placement hosts.
workflows.description: Determines the VM's real HA owner, replicates the latest changes to the chosen placement host, and relocates the VM there. The application is briefly unavailable while the VM restarts. Staging VMs on the new owner are evicted.

workflows.title: Change placement
workflows.summary: Add or remove the hosts a production VM replicates to and may run on.
workflows.description: Adds placement hosts (replicating the VM there before HA may use them) or removes them (never the live owner, keeping at least two). Detects and finishes a partial earlier change.

workflows.title: Grow production disk
workflows.summary: Grow a production VM's root disk online.
workflows.description: Calculates how much the VM's root zvol may grow while every placement pool keeps 10% free, grows it on the live owner, replicates the new size, and grows the guest's filesystem online.

params.label: Dry run (show the growth limit only)

workflows.title: Set up SSH access
workflows.summary: Pin a guest's host key and configure ssh <alias> through a jump host.
workflows.description: Reads the guest's SSH host key through the guest agent, picks a jump host, writes a strict managed block to ~/.ssh/config and known_hosts, and proves ssh works.

workflows.title: Deploy example todo app
workflows.summary: Build and install the example todo app on a production VM.
workflows.description: Builds the example todo app (Rust, SQLite) on this workstation, then installs it on a production VM as a systemd service that serves HTTPS with your Cloudflare origin certificate. Needs the Rust x86_64-unknown-linux-musl target and musl-tools. An example deployment, not a general deployer.

workflows.title: Monitored services
workflows.summary: View and add or remove the systemd services and certificate files a production VM's monitor watches.
workflows.description: Reads /etc/app-ha-monitor/guest.json on the VM over ssh prodN with each watched service's state and certificate's expiry, then lets you change the lists. Validates every unit and certificate on the VM before saving. Never touches the registry or the QDevice.

workflows.title: Add prod-linked Staging VM
workflows.summary: Create a staging VM as a linked clone of a production VM's current state.
workflows.description: Snapshots a production VM, waits for the snapshot to replicate to a standby host, and creates a stopped stageNprodN linked clone there with a new machine identity. When the production VM already has staging VMs, it lists them and offers to share one of their snapshots instead of taking a new one. Optionally starts it and sets up SSH. Start with a dry run.

params.label: Sanitizer script
params.help: Optional local Bash script run as root inside the clone before its networking starts.

workflows.title: Instant Restore to Backup-Linked Staging VM
workflows.summary: Boot one of a production VM's restore points as a staging VM within about a minute; its data stays on PBS.
workflows.description: Creates a disposable staging VM in the production VM's lowest free staging slot (stageKprodN, its address and FQDN) from one of its restore points on PBS. The restore point is mapped read-only from PBS on a host of the production VM's placement where no production VM runs; a local copy-on-write overlay takes the VM's writes, and is patched offline with the slot's identity (hostname, network, machine-id, SSH host keys, staging root password, and an optional sanitizer) before the first boot. The restore point's data is never copied, so reads of data the VM has not changed come from PBS and are slower than local disk. It counts toward the host's staging quota, the production VM need not be running, and it is evicted like any staging VM when a production VM starts on its host, and also when its PBS mapping dies, for example when its host reboots. Remove it with Remove staging VM.

params.label: Restore point
params.help: Such as vm/100/2026-10-27T14:50:01Z; chosen from the restore points of registered production VMs when empty.

params.label: Sanitizer script
params.help: Optional local Bash script run as root inside the VM before its networking starts.

params.label: Host
params.help: Chosen when more than one host is eligible.

workflows.title: Remove staging VM
workflows.summary: Destroy a staging VM with its clone or overlay; the production VM and its restore points are untouched.
workflows.description: Permanently removes a staging VM's VM and disks. For a prod-linked staging VM, also its linked clone and its source snapshot unless another staging VM still shares it (a shared snapshot is deleted with the last staging VM using it). For a backup-linked staging VM, also its overlay and PBS mapping; its restore point stays on PBS. Production itself is never touched.

params.label: Dry run (show the destruction plan only)

workflows.title: Add Proxmox host
workflows.summary: Install and join a new Proxmox host using a customized installer ISO.
workflows.description: Builds a customized Proxmox installer ISO, guides the installation, converts storage, joins the host to the cluster through the control node, and reconciles the QDevice. Long-running and interactive.
workflows.platform_note: Requires a Debian-based Linux x86_64 workstation, because BMAC must build a customized Proxmox installer ISO with Proxmox's amd64-only Debian tool.

choices.label: Run mirror-member and final boot tests

workflows.title: Remove Proxmox host
workflows.summary: Remove a host gracefully, or forcefully when it is permanently dead.
workflows.description: Removes a host gracefully when it can be contacted and nothing depends on it, or forcefully when it cannot be contacted and has been permanently disconnected. Forced removal narrows affected production placement and destroys related staging VMs.
workflows.platform_note: Takes the same workstation flock as host setup, so it runs on Linux workstations only.

workflows.title: Update cluster runtime
workflows.summary: Deploy this checkout's BMAC runtime helpers and hooks to every host, and inject monitor daemons.
workflows.description: Stages and validates the BMAC runtime bundle on every online host, installs it atomically, verifies it cluster-wide, and rolls back on failure, then upgrades cloudflared one host at a time without interrupting ingress. Updates BMAC code and cloudflared, not other Proxmox packages.

params.label: Leave every host's cloudflared version as it is

workflows.title: Sync cluster with cluster.conf
workflows.summary: Push cluster.conf's VM slots, guest gateway, transfer caps, and tunnel settings to every host.
workflows.description: Shows which hosts differ from cluster.conf and their moxN.conf, then (without dry run) updates the registry's VM slots, the installed cluster.conf, every host's shared guest gateway, egress NAT, fallback routing and transfer cap, revalidates the egress probe targets, reinstalls the tunnel credentials, and brings every tunnel config up to date, restarting replicas one host at a time. Refuses slot changes that would move a registered VM. Rarely needed: run it after editing those settings.

workflows.title: Add mirrored vdev
workflows.summary: Add two new disks to a host's rpool as one mirror.
workflows.description: Lists unused disks, asks for two of matching capacity, prepares them (with LUKS at the host console on encrypted hosts), updates crypttab and initramfs, and adds them to rpool. Erases the chosen disks.

workflows.title: Replace mirror member
workflows.summary: Put a replacement disk into a degraded rpool mirror.
workflows.description: Copies the surviving member's partition layout to a replacement disk (and its ESP for the boot mirror), encrypts it on encrypted hosts, and starts resilvering. The failed disk must already be pulled.

workflows.title: Decommission a vdev
workflows.summary: Trim, replicate, scrub, then evacuate one non-boot vdev from rpool.
workflows.description: Requires that no related staging VM exists, trims affected production guests, forces their replication, scrubs rpool, and starts removing one eligible non-boot vdev. Finish with Inventory disks.

workflows.title: Simulate disk failure
workflows.summary: TEST AID: fail and erase one rpool mirror member.
workflows.description: Takes one member of a healthy two-way mirror offline and, after a second confirmation, erases its disk so the replacement workflow can be tested. Destroys the data on that disk.

workflows.title: Add QDevice
workflows.summary: Add an external tie-breaking vote to an even-sized cluster.
workflows.description: Checks that the cluster needs a QDevice, verifies SSH to the prepared QDevice machine, installs corosync-qnetd there, pins its host key on every host, and runs pvecm qdevice setup.
workflows.platform_note: Takes the same workstation flock as host setup, so it runs on Linux workstations only.

workflows.title: Remove QDevice
workflows.summary: Remove the QDevice gracefully, or evict a failed one forcefully.
workflows.description: Removes a reachable QDevice gracefully and uninstalls its software. When it is inaccessible, offers to evict it forcefully without contacting it, after you confirm it was removed from Tailscale.
workflows.platform_note: Takes the same workstation flock as host setup, so it runs on Linux workstations only.

params.label: QDevice SSH host
params.help: Defaults to PROXMOX_QDEVICE_HOST from config/cluster.conf.

workflows.title: Health-check probes
workflows.summary: View and change the HTTPS probes the QDevice runs through Cloudflare for each production VM.
workflows.description: Shows every production VM's ingress health-check probe and the QDevice's latest result, and edits one VM's probe (FQDNs, path, expected status and text). The probe runs once from the QDevice before it is saved in the registry and installed in the QDevice's monitor config.

params.label: Production VM
params.help: The VM whose probe to change; asked for when empty.

workflows.title: List backups
workflows.summary: PBS storage, retention policy, each production VM's backup schedule, and BMAC's restore points.
workflows.description: Reads through one reachable member whether the bmac-pbs storage is set up and active, the retention policy the PBS server's prune job applies (when the cluster's token can read it), each production VM's backup job and newest backup, and every restore point BMAC made, with its protection and encryption key. Changes nothing.

workflows.title: Setup PBS
workflows.summary: Connect the cluster to its Proxmox Backup Server with an encryption key and your master public key.
workflows.description: Checks from a cluster host that the PBS certificate matches PROXMOX_PBS_FINGERPRINT, that the token holds Datastore.Backup and Datastore.Audit on its namespace (warning about any privilege that could delete backups), and whether the namespace already holds backups. Then adds the PVE storage bmac-pbs with a new encryption key, or with the existing key when backups exist, and your master public key, and saves a copy of the key for you to store offline. When bmac-pbs already exists, it only saves the key copy.

params.label: Master public key
params.help: PEM file of the master public key. Defaults to pbs-master-public.pem in the configuration directory, and is asked for when that file does not exist.

params.label: Existing encryption key
params.help: Use this key instead of generating one; asked for when the namespace already holds backups.

workflows.title: Backup schedule
workflows.summary: Back a production VM up every 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours, or disable or remove its backup job.
workflows.description: Creates or changes the production VM's PVE backup job bmac-prodN: snapshot mode with the guest agent's filesystem freeze, fleecing on local storage, BMAC's notes on every backup, and no bandwidth limit unless you set one. The job runs on whichever host runs the VM. Disabling keeps the job; removing deletes it, and the VM's existing backups stay on PBS. How long backups are kept is set by the PBS server's prune job.

params.label: Production VM
params.help: Asked for when empty.

params.label: Back up every
params.help: Asked for when empty.

params.label: Upload limit (MiB/s)
params.help: Optional; backups are not limited by default.

workflows.title: Back up now
workflows.summary: Back a production VM up to PBS now, with the same settings as its scheduled backups.
workflows.description: Starts a backup of the production VM as a PVE task on the host that runs it, in snapshot mode while the VM keeps running, and shows its progress. The task finishes even if this workstation disconnects. The new restore point counts toward the PBS prune job's keep-last.

params.label: Production VM
params.help: Asked for when empty.

workflows.title: Protect a restore point
workflows.summary: Keep a restore point however old it gets, or clear that protection again.
workflows.description: Sets or clears the protected flag of one of BMAC's restore points on PBS. The PBS prune job never removes a protected restore point; once its protection is cleared, the normal retention policy applies to it again. Protected restore points use PBS space until then.

params.label: Restore point
params.help: Such as vm/100/2026-10-27T14:50:01Z; chosen from a list when empty.

params.label: Action
params.help: The opposite of the current state when empty.

workflows.title: Full Restore to Existing VM
workflows.summary: Return a production VM to one of its own restore points, down until the restore finishes; everything written since is lost.
workflows.description: Restores a production VM's disks and settings from one of its restore points on PBS, keeping its identity (VMID, name, MAC, address, tags, lifecycle hook) and, unless you choose others, its vCPUs and RAM. Offers a safety backup of the current state first. Stops the VM through HA, deletes its replication jobs and replicas, restores on the VM's host, starts it again through HA, and recreates replication with a full initial sync, during which the VM cannot fail over. Requires a typed confirmation.

params.label: Production VM
params.help: Asked for when empty.

params.label: Restore point
params.help: Such as vm/100/2026-10-27T14:50:01Z; chosen from the VM's restore points when empty.

params.label: vCPUs
params.help: Default: the VM's current vCPUs.

params.label: RAM (GiB)
params.help: Default: the VM's current RAM.

params.label: Replication interval (minutes)
params.help: For the recreated replication jobs. Default: the current schedule.

params.label: Safety backup first
params.help: Asked for when empty.

choices.label: Back up the current state first

workflows.title: Instant Restore to Existing VM
workflows.summary: Return a production VM to one of its own restore points, down only until it boots again; everything written since is lost.
workflows.description: Instant Restore to New Permanent VM's method for an existing production VM: it returns to one of its restore points, keeping its identity, its current settings, and, unless you choose others, its vCPUs and RAM, but is down only until it boots again, usually a minute or two. Offers a safety backup of the current state first. Stops the VM through HA, deletes its replication jobs and replicas, frees its disk, and starts it through HA from a local overlay over the restore point mapped read-only from PBS. Reads of data not yet copied are slower. Meanwhile the restore point's in-use data is copied into its own disk, the running disk is switched to it without a restart, the disk is grown back to its registered size, and replication is recreated with a full initial sync. Until then it cannot fail over and cannot be the source of a prod-linked staging VM. Run it again for the same VM to resume. Requires a typed confirmation.

params.label: Production VM
params.help: Asked for when empty.

params.label: Restore point
params.help: Such as vm/100/2026-10-27T14:50:01Z; chosen from the VM's restore points when empty. A resumed restore keeps the one it started from.

params.label: vCPUs
params.help: Default: the VM's current vCPUs.

params.label: RAM (GiB)
params.help: Default: the VM's current RAM.

params.label: Replication interval (minutes)
params.help: For the recreated replication jobs. Default: the current schedule.

params.label: Safety backup first
params.help: Asked for when empty.

choices.label: Back up the current state first

params.label: Copy delay (seconds, developer)
params.help: Developer option: keep the VM running from its restore point on PBS this long (at most 3600) before its data is copied, to try it there.

workflows.title: Full Restore to New VM
workflows.summary: Create a new production VM from a restore point, for example on a rebuilt cluster.
workflows.description: Creates a production VM from one of BMAC's restore points on PBS: it gets the restore point's own slot (name and address) and VMID when they are free, otherwise new ones, and asks for the purpose, FQDN, aliases, placement, vCPUs and RAM (defaulting to the restore point's). The restore runs stopped; the root disk is patched offline with its hostname, network, this cluster's root password and administrator SSH keys, and, in a different slot, a new machine-id and SSH host keys. Then, as for a new production VM, the guest is verified and gets its networking, replication, HA, Cloudflare Tunnel routes, and monitoring. Rerun with the same purpose to resume.

params.label: Restore point
params.help: Such as vm/100/2026-10-27T14:50:01Z; chosen from every restore point this cluster can decrypt when empty.

params.label: vCPUs
params.help: Default: the restore point's vCPUs.

params.label: RAM (GiB)
params.help: Default: the restore point's RAM.

workflows.title: Instant Restore to New Permanent VM
workflows.summary: Create a new production VM from a restore point that serves its FQDNs within minutes, while its disk is copied.
workflows.description: Full Restore to New VM without the wait: the same slot, VMID, form, and identity patching, but the VM boots within minutes from its restore point mapped read-only from PBS, behind a local overlay that takes its writes, and its FQDNs are routed to it at once. Reads of data not yet copied come from PBS and are slower. Meanwhile only the restore point's in-use data is copied into the VM's own zvol; then the running disk is switched to the zvol without a restart, the overlay and mapping are removed, and the VM gets its final networking, replication, HA, and monitoring. Until that switch it cannot be the source of a prod-linked staging VM. Rerun with the same purpose to resume, also after a host reboot during the copy.

params.label: Restore point
params.help: Such as vm/100/2026-10-27T14:50:01Z; chosen from every restore point this cluster can decrypt when empty.

params.label: vCPUs
params.help: Default: the restore point's vCPUs.

params.label: RAM (GiB)
params.help: Default: the restore point's RAM.

params.label: Copy delay (seconds, developer)
params.help: Developer option: keep the VM running from its restore point on PBS this long (at most 3600) before its data is copied, to try it there.
